key_insight: This paper introduces Differentiable Gaussian Dynamics (DGD), a way to learn how individual-level response differences roll up into population-level collective behavior. It makes aggregate count data useful for predicting both current response distributions and future dynamics.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of learning collective response dynamics from only aggregated observations, where individual heterogeneity, contact opportunities, and past experience all shape behavior but are not directly observed.
method: Represents heterogeneous response propensities with a Gaussian mixture model.
Uses differentiable aggregation to connect contact intensity and behavioral patterns to observed population counts.
Learns a dynamic mapping from aggregate observations to future collective behavior in an end-to-end differentiable framework.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a principled way to model population dynamics when only coarse aggregate data is available. It is especially useful for forecasting, behavioral modeling, and other settings where individual-level labels are missing but group-level trends matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing individual propensities flowing into aggregate counts and future predictions
Gaussian mixture plot illustrating heterogeneous response distributions
Time-series chart comparing observed vs. predicted collective dynamics
Icon-based schematic for contact intensity, behavioral response, and accumulated experience
paper_title: Learning Collective Dynamics with Differentiable Gaussian Representations
paper_authors: Jianxiang Ma, Mingfu Zhang, Xiaocui Yang, Yichen Gao, Junzhao Huang
